summary: Input and Textarea gain `surface: "page" | "chrome"`, and the field fill becomes a GROUND x STATE matrix (ADR 0017). A review flagged the editor inspector for drawing its fields on `bg-sunken` — the value a DISABLED field is filled with. The reading was half right: the drawing was correct and the library was incomplete. Those fields sit on a `bg-elevated` panel, not on the page, and a field is a well cut from whatever contains it, so the same fill means different things on different floors. `resolve.ts` already said so — the comment above `--ui-bg-field` reads 'a field is RECESSED from whatever contains it' — while the derivation reads the page, so the role only held when the page was the container and there was no name for the other case. Four roles now: `--ui-bg-field` / `--ui-bg-field-disabled` on the page, `--ui-bg-field-chrome` / `--ui-bg-field-chrome-disabled` on chrome. `--ui-bg-field-disabled` and `--ui-bg-field-chrome` resolve to the SAME VALUE in theme zero and that is the finding rather than a slip: neutral-90 under a white page reads as unavailable, the identical neutral-90 inside a neutral-95 inspector reads as a well you can type into. So the assertion is not that the four differ — it is that each PAIR separates on its own ground, in both schemes across every stress seed, plus the chrome field reading as a well against the panel. The mechanism of the original collision was a state pointing at a surface role (`isDisabled && "bg-sunken"`); both components now take the enabled and disabled fills TOGETHER from one map, so they cannot be picked apart. The ground is a prop rather than inference because a panel knows it is a panel and an input does not — and the tempting alternative, having chrome surfaces re-point `--ui-bg-field` for their subtree, breaks on exactly the components that need it most, since a Popover, Menu or Select panel is portalled to document.body and inherits nothing. Every value is floored by measurement rather than authored as a step, so a brand whose surfaces sit close together cannot collapse a pair. Light is unchanged; two dark baselines moved, and the dark disabled fill now separates from its field at 1.237 where it used to manage 1.127.

migration.manual: Nothing to change at a call site: `surface` defaults to "page" and every light value is byte-identical. Pass surface="chrome" for a field inside an inspector, island, drawer or bottom sheet — anything floored with bg-elevated — and both its enabled and disabled fills move together. In dark, a DISABLED field's fill changes from #282522 to #2F2C29; if you pinned that value in a test or an override, it moves. Two dark visual baselines were regenerated. Select, Multiselect and Combobox still fill from bg-field directly and want the same prop.
